record.title: IndustrialVLA-Bench separates clean simulation scores from robustness and instruction sensitivity
record.summary: An October 2026 preprint evaluates six released vision-language-action and world-action robot policies across clean LIBERO tasks, visual/embodiment perturbations, instruction paraphrases and observed runtime costs. Across the six systems, the paper reports only a 1.58-point spread on clean LIBERO but larger spreads on visual robustness and paraphrase success. Three systems are marked protocol-faithful; near-reproduction and pending-verification rows remain diagnostic and are excluded from strict comparisons. Results are limited to selected checkpoints in LIBERO-family simulation, not real-robot performance or causal architectural comparisons.
organizations: Southern University of Science and Technology

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: Across six selected released policies, the authors report a 1.58-point range in clean LIBERO averages versus 14.62 points in non-language robustness and 31.08 points in LIBERO-Para paraphrase success. Restricting the comparison to the three protocol-faithful systems preserves the separation.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The paper distinguishes protocol-faithful, near-reproduction and pending-verification results; only protocol-faithful rows are used for strict comparisons. It does not infer causal effects of VLA versus WAM architecture from the checkpoint set.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The paper reports observed latency, peak VRAM, runtime mode and setup burden for the evaluated checkpoints, while cautioning that those observations are not controlled intrinsic efficiency rankings.

evidence_gaps.description: No independent reproduction was performed. Three of six reported systems are not protocol-faithful, and the paper’s strict cross-model comparison covers only the other three.
The evaluation uses LIBERO-family simulation and six purposively selected checkpoints; no real-robot task, broader benchmark census or architecture-causal comparison is established.

brief.importance_rationale: If the reported diagnostic separation persists, robot-policy selection would need to consider visual robustness, language sensitivity and execution cost alongside clean success. A 5 reflects a useful evaluation contribution across six released checkpoints, bounded by simulation-only scope and three protocol-faithful systems.
limitations: The paper reports simulation-only results on a purposive set of six released checkpoints; it does not claim coverage of all open robot policies.
Three entries are protocol-faithful; one is near-reproduction and two are pending verification. Strict claims should use only the faithful subset.
Latency and memory are observed runtime profiles, not controlled cross-model efficiency measurements.
Results do not establish causal advantages of VLA or WAM architectures, real-world robustness or safety.
No independent reproduction was performed in this review.
organizations: Southern University of Science and Technology
brief.summary: An October 2026 preprint evaluates six released vision-language-action and world-action robot policies across clean LIBERO tasks, visual/embodiment perturbations, instruction paraphrases and observed runtime costs. Across the six systems, the paper reports only a 1.58-point spread on clean LIBERO but larger spreads on visual robustness and paraphrase success. Three systems are marked protocol-faithful; near-reproduction and pending-verification rows remain diagnostic and are excluded from strict comparisons. Results are limited to selected checkpoints in LIBERO-family simulation, not real-robot performance or causal architectural comparisons.

technical.claimed_result: Across six systems, clean LIBERO averages span 1.58 points, robustness summaries span 14.62 points and paraphrase results span 31.08 points; the diagnostic spread persists among three protocol-faithful systems.
technical.demonstrated_result: The paper defines an explicit checkpoint and comparability protocol and reports three-run benchmark summaries. Numerical outcomes remain author-reported and unreplicated here.
technical.mechanism: A shared evaluation schema reports clean LIBERO success, visual/embodiment perturbation robustness, semantics-preserving instruction paraphrase sensitivity, and runtime/reproducibility status as separate axes.
technical.regime: Six selected open robot-policy checkpoints in LIBERO, LIBERO-Plus and LIBERO-Para simulation; three protocol-faithful, one near-reproduction, two pending verification.
technical.reproducibility: Paper describes an author-linked GitHub harness and evaluation records. Repository inspected at index level; no code/model execution or independent reproduction was performed.
technical.strongest_baseline: Three protocol-faithful released checkpoints compared under fixed checkpoint/inference configuration and three run-level seeds on LIBERO-family protocols.

brief.title: IndustrialVLA-Bench separates clean simulation scores from robustness and instruction sensitivity
brief.why_it_matters: A clean benchmark score may hide important differences in robustness, instruction handling and deployability for executable robot policies. This evaluation makes those dimensions and evidence tiers visible together, while explicitly limiting strict comparisons to runs that meet its protocol-fidelity criteria.
